feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications role: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/operations leadership. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style and grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director, which strengthens credibility.  
- Strong domain fit: digital strategy, Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics, governance, and multimedia are all well evidenced.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which improves impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond scope metrics: include performance improvements, engagement gains, efficiency savings, revenue/supporting impact, or campaign outcomes.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidating these sections would improve structure and readability.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; standardize punctuation in lists (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “French (basic working proficiency).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a clearer leadership/value angle would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with current market positioning: “Digital communications and strategy leader” rather than “professional.”
- Replace broad lists with sharper outcomes-oriented framing, e.g. emphasize leading digital transformation, modernizing platforms, and building scalable editorial/communications systems for mission-driven organizations.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and scalable editorial workflows that improve coordination and execution. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating complex technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” appears here and is reinforced throughout experience; keep it once for emphasis.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening wording and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, higher-impact phrasing: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS and web operations • Editorial systems and governance
- Replace vague items with sharper terms: Analytics and performance reporting • Workflow architecture and process improvement • Stakeholder and cross-functional alignment
- Keep advocacy/media strengths, but streamline: Policy and advocacy communications • Multimedia and live event production
- Consider reducing to 6–8 items to avoid reading like a duplicate skills list and to better match senior-level positioning

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “stakeholder & cross-department coordination,” and “policy & advocacy communication” repeat language already used in the header and Soft Skills.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “data analytics & reporting” overlap with Topline Skills and Technical + IT; use broader leadership framing here instead.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical breadth, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with your NACo entries on governance, workflows, and web operations. Tighten it around what is new here: freelance leadership, Drupal campaign builds, and the AI-enabled search initiative.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type: “Embedded full-time as a strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, campaign platform development, and enterprise web improvement.”
- Replace broad bullets with sharper action/result phrasing: “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including microsite templates, modular content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Combine overlapping systems/governance points: “Improved cross-channel content operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Keep the AI work prominent and outcome-oriented: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.” Add metrics if available (sites, users, time saved, adoption).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats NACo language; avoid using all three separately here.
- “Technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties” is vague and low-impact unless quantified.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like and the bullets emphasized outcomes, team leadership, and transformation over channel inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a tighter scope statement: “Led NACo’s digital communications function, managing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a national association.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Directed redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: growth/engagement for email and social, cost savings or production volume from the in-house studio, reporting speed/adoption from analytics improvements.
- Tighten phrasing: use strong verbs like “modernized,” “scaled,” “launched,” and “standardized”; avoid repeating “Led/Directed” in every bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance/publishing workflows” overlaps with the current consulting role and prior NACo role; keep this version focused on enterprise-scale transformation.
- Video leadership overlaps with earlier NACo entries; emphasize building the studio, not recurring video production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good scope, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later NACo director role and earlier digital media role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, editorial operations, and any concrete growth or efficiency gains.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social, and video, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial planning.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching [X]+ county officials and public-sector stakeholders” and “Produced a weekly advocacy video update that established video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter audience size, open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, or workflow turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the last two bullets into one impact statement: “Built editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved coordination across communications, advocacy, and program teams and increased consistency of digital output.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning/coordination” and “improved publishing workflows” duplicate themes already covered in the 2022–2024 NACo role.
- Weekly video work may overlap with the 2015–2018 role unless you clarify expansion/ownership at this level.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership and governance rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Swap “audience-focused content planning” for “audience-centered content strategy” to sound more senior and outcome-oriented.
- Consider “content operations” instead of “editorial systems” to better match recent experience building workflows, governance, and enterprise publishing structures.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section to scale/results rather than here; Topline Skills should stay concise and non-duplicative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeats “Multi-channel communication” in Core Competencies.
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “public-sector and advocacy messaging” are already strongly covered in the header summary.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s currently a mixed keyword list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. Make it more selective and impact-oriented, emphasizing the most relevant recent strengths from the 2022–present roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • SharePoint & Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery
- Lead with Drupal/CMS modernization and AI-enabled search, since those are most supported by recent experience.
- Combine “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” into one concise phrase; keep older/secondary platforms later in the line.
- If space allows, replace one generic term with a stronger outcome-linked phrase, e.g., “enterprise web migration support” or “modular microsite development.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, API integrations, Airtable” are already repeated in “Technical + IT”; avoid mirroring the same list verbatim.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack that aligns well with the 2022–present leadership roles, but it reads as a raw list. Make it more outcome-oriented and strategic so it reinforces seniority rather than just platform familiarity.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + business value, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, and performance optimization.”
- Group tools more cleanly: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing such as “executive dashboarding” or “decision-ready reporting.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity; KPI design, executive dashboarding, SEO and digital performance analysis.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; this item should add specificity, not repeat that phrase.
- The NACo Director role already mentions expanding analytics infrastructure, so avoid overexplaining tools here without emphasizing insight/decision-making.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more senior, specific, and tied to recent delivery strengths rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools/tasks to capability: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • Studio buildout and operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event execution”
- If space allows, add scope/level language: “In-house studio leadership” or “end-to-end event production” to signal ownership, not just participation.
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the Director-level experience.
- Keep only the most differentiating terms; “Livestreaming” + “Hybrid and virtual event production” may be enough without separate lower-level phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partially duplicates “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; use one section for broad category, the other for specifics.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” support the NACo studio bullet, so avoid repeating studio buildout language elsewhere.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” In a recent, impact-led CV, this item should either be tightened or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “CMS Platforms” for brevity.
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add proficiency context instead of a plain list: “Drupal (enterprise migration, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If no context can be added here, keep this item very short and let recent work experience carry the impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is largely duplicated by “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus broader technical capabilities.
- “GitHub Pages” may be lower-value/noise unless it played a meaningful role in recent work.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should emphasize current, implementation-level tools and trim older/basic terms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and recency: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery; API integrations; tag management; edge/serverless scripting; deployment automation”
- Consider replacing “HTML5 • CSS3” with “HTML • CSS” for concision; version numbers add little value here.
- If accurate, add outcome-oriented qualifiers tied to recent work: “Cloudflare Workers for lightweight web functionality,” “GitHub Actions for deployment/workflow automation,” “Google Tag Manager for analytics/event tracking.”
- Order by relevance to current roles: JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • HTML/CSS • jQuery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations • Workflow automation”); avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- “Workflow automation” is already covered elsewhere, so keep this item focused on coding/implementation tools only.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. Since recent roles emphasize systems architecture and cross-team operations, this item should signal automation/building capability, not just collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Split into two lines to sharpen relevance:  
  Automation & workflow tools: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier  
  Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp
- Move Slack and Teams out unless they are central to workflow design; they read as basic workplace tools and dilute the section.
- Consider adding a qualifier if accurate: “workflow design, automations, and team operating systems” to frame these as implementation tools, not familiarity only.
- If space allows, prioritize strongest/recent tools first and add scope only if measurable, e.g., “Airtable systems” or “cross-team workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap heavily; consider trimming to the 2–3 most used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal level of use. Since recent roles emphasize email leadership, this should read as a focused platform stack, not just a list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing, CRM & Community Platforms
- Tighten platform names for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add level/context in brief parentheticals: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys (campaign automation/CRM) • Higher Logic (member email/community) • Mailchimp (newsletter campaigns)
- Keep it platform-only; let work experience carry outcomes rather than forcing metrics into a skills line

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated email leadership already shown in NACo roles; avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here
- “Engagement Systems” is somewhat vague and may duplicate broader “Multi-channel communications” language elsewhere

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational contributions, promotion, and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outcomes if available: website refresh size/traffic impact, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience growth, email/social performance, or team/process efficiencies.
- Clarify your ownership: replace “contributed to” with stronger verbs like “supported launch of,” “produced,” “coordinated,” or “standardized,” depending on actual responsibility.
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, standardizing workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this entry as the launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete outputs, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles that already cover broader content production.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Split research/program support from multimedia work so the scope is clearer.
- Replace generic phrases like “contributed to” and “supporting organizational programs” with stronger verbs and specific deliverables.
- If possible, add volume or reach: number of projects, episodes, stakeholders, or policy/program teams supported.

Suggested edit:
- Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.
- Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, translating research and policy work into accessible formats.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, recording coordination, and production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and innovation/research support.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
